risk_if_not_implemented: Without Continuous Authentication, credentials may be phished, replayed, guessed or stolen, allowing unauthorized actors to authenticate as trusted identities. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Anomalous Behavior
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and/or User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solutions to detect and respond to anomalous behavior that could indicate account compromise or other malicious activities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Anomalous Behavior (MON-16) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Continuous Authentication (IAC-42) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Adaptive Identification & Authentication
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to allow individuals to utilize alternative methods of authentication under specific circumstances or situations.
compensating_control_2.justification: Adaptive Identification & Authentication (IAC-41) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Continuous Authentication (IAC-42) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
